findings.title: Vault Program Does Not Support SPL Token 2022 Transfers and Initialization
findings.description:
The vault program fails to support SPL Token 2022 for both initialization and token transfers. This is because the program hardcodes the use of the legacy SPL Token program ID (`TokenkegQfeZyiNwAJbNbGKPFXCWuBvf9Ss623VQ5DA`) in the `process_mint` instruction instead of dynamically accepting the SPL Token 2022 program ID (`TokenzQdBNbLqP5VEhdkAS6EPFLC1PHnBqCXEpPxuEb`). Additionally, during vault initialization in `process_initialize_vault`, the `load_token_program` function strictly validates that the provided token program ID matches the legacy SPL Token ID, rejecting SPL Token 2022 outright.

The root cause is the hardcoded dependency on `spl_token::id()` and the lack of conditional logic to handle both SPL Token and SPL Token 2022 program variants. This design decision prevents interoperability with modern token standards on Solana.

An attacker or malicious actor cannot directly exploit this for financial gain, but legitimate users attempting to interact with the vault using SPL Token 2022 will have their transactions fail, leading to a denial of service for those token types.

The impact is that the vault program cannot be used with SPL Token 2022 assets, undermining the project's stated goal of supporting both SPL Token and SPL Token 2022 standards. This limits usability and adoption for users relying on the newer token standard.
